result:
The full Netflix clone is built and the validator passes: **14/14 api_smoke checks**, and all 8 business-chain steps succeed, including the cross-user isolation probe. That was validation call 2 of 20.

**What's there**
- **Stack:** `docker/docker-compose.yml` starts `database` (Postgres 16), `backend` (FastAPI, port 8000) and `frontend` (React/Vite served by nginx, port 3000; it forwards `/api` and `/auth` to the backend).
- **Data:** seeded from `titles.json` with the real posters, backdrops and trailer clips. There are 22 genres derived from the titles, numbered episodes for each series, and a demo account `demo@netflix.local` / `netflix123` with Demo, Alex and Kids profiles.
- **API:** all 17 endpoints at the exact paths, using the `{item}`/`{items}` response shapes, returning 401 without a token, and checking passwords properly. I added a few extras: edit/delete profile, save watch progress, a languages list, and `PUT /api/my-list/{id}` ("move to top").
- **Per-profile privacy:** the frontend sends the active profile in an `X-Profile-Id` header and the backend checks that profile belongs to the logged-in user (403 otherwise). Kids profiles only see Family/Animation titles.
- **Screens:** all 13, plus search, account and a not-found page. That includes the title-detail modal with a season selector, the rate dialog, the account menu, the card hover preview, ranked Top 10 rows, and a full player (seek bar, ±10s, volume, next episode, episodes panel, audio/subtitles panel, fullscreen, back) that saves progress so you can resume.
- **Testing:** besides the validator, I ran the backend against a local Postgres and drove the UI in headless Chromium through signup, adding profiles, My List per profile, rating, search, genre and language browsing, notifications, the player and sign-out. There were no console errors, and the screenshots match the reference layouts closely.

**Known gaps**
- The dataset has no runtimes, cast or episode data, and these are filled honestly rather than invented:
  - Durations shown are the real trailer-clip lengths (7–15 seconds).
  - Episodes are named "Episode N", and only Episode 1 carries the show's real synopsis.
  - There's no cast line in the detail modal.
- There are no games in the data, so the Games page shows an empty state; "Coming This Week" and the Dubbing/Subtitles language options do the same.
- Title logos are drawn as text in the Anton font, since no logo artwork was provided.
- One dataset row is skipped: an adult title with no poster or genre.
- I couldn't see video actually play: the headless browser here can't decode H.264, so the player shows an error message in that case. A normal desktop browser should play the clips.
- The validator lists 4 endpoints as "not answering 2xx". Those are its empty-body probes, which correctly get 422, or 404 when deleting something that isn't in the list. It doesn't fail any check.

The README explains how to run it and regenerate the seed data.
